findings.where: 'Where we're starting' section: the three destination cards (Canggu, Uluwatu, Kuta Lombok), each with its 'Best hostels >' line
findings.fault: The cards look clickable but do nothing. Each is a white card with a heavy shadow and a hover rule, and it carries a 'Best hostels' line in the link colour with a chevron. The parts map shows that neither the cards nor the 'Best hostels' lines are links. This is where the page should send visitors to the destination guides, and the route stops here. 'Explore destinations' and the 'Destinations' nav link both lead to this dead end.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who taps 'Best hostels' under Canggu to see the guide. Nothing happens, and they leave thinking the site is broken or empty. The founder would object too, since sending visitors to the guides is one of the page's three jobs and the SEO guide routes are the only content it has.

findings.where: Nav 'How we rank' (desktop), and the footer links 'Privacy', 'Terms', 'How we rank' and 'Report content'
findings.fault: These are links in name only. Each one points back to this same page, so a click goes nowhere. 'How we rank' is the only place to read about merit ranking, which is the claim the hero makes. Privacy is missing on a page that asks for people's email addresses.
findings.who_objects: A careful first-time visitor who wants to know how 'ranked on merit alone' works, or what happens to their email, before writing in. Each dead link makes the merit claim look hollow. A visitor who wants to report something also has no way to do it.

findings.where: Hero: the coral primary button 'Email luc@mantahostels.com for launch news'
findings.fault: The page's main action is a mailto link. On a desktop with no mail app set up, a click does nothing or opens an unwanted setup screen. Where it does work, the visitor has to write and send their own email, and nothing tells them what to put in it. Nothing on the page confirms they are now on the launch list.
findings.who_objects: A visitor on a laptop who uses webmail clicks the main button and nothing usable opens. A phone visitor lands in a blank draft and gives up. Either way the founder loses the sign-up the page exists to collect.

findings.where: Destination cards: the 2 px purple outline drawn on all three cards at rest
findings.fault: Every card wears a bright outline in a colour found nowhere else on the page. That reads as a selected or focused state, or as visited-link purple. Because all three show it at once, it suggests the visitor has already picked or visited them.
findings.who_objects: A visitor scanning the cards can't tell whether a card is selected, focused or already seen. The look borrows the selected-state edge that a filter or focus ring uses, when the cards are plain destinations.

findings.where: Desktop nav: 'Destinations' (no underline) next to 'How we rank' (underlined)
findings.fault: The two nav links do the same job but look different. Only one is underlined, so it looks either like the only real link or like a current-page marker. It is neither.
findings.who_objects: A visitor reading the nav may take 'Destinations' for a label rather than a link, or think they are already on 'How we rank'.
